sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: There are certain issues where we just don't see eye to eye with people on the other side of the political aisle.
sentences.zh: 在某些议题上，我们与政治立场对立的人确实无法达成共识。

sentences.en: Often, it feels like we don't just disagree over policy.
sentences.zh: 通常，这种感觉不仅仅是因为我们在政策上存在分歧。

sentences.en: We can't even agree on the facts.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至无法在事实层面达成一致。

sentences.en: I think people are mostly just set in their ways.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们大多只是固执己见。

sentences.en: I would say I'm right objectively.
sentences.zh: 我会说我是客观正确的。

sentences.en: The facts prove that there is global warming.
sentences.zh: 事实证明全球变暖是存在的。

sentences.en: I don't know how you can dispute it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你怎么能反驳这一点。

sentences.en: But everybody thinks they're right.
sentences.zh: 但每个人都认为自己是对的。

sentences.en: I think they're wrong.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们错了。

sentences.en: I think they're making a huge mistake.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们犯了一个巨大的错误。

sentences.en: Because security has to be a very big issue.
sentences.zh: 因为安全必须是一个非常重大的议题。

sentences.en: My guest today has spent years studying the way we process information and why we often reach biased conclusions.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾花了多年时间研究我们处理信息的方式，以及为什么我们经常得出带有偏见的结论。

sentences.en: She says it's surprisingly difficult for us to change one another's minds, no matter how much data we present.
sentences.zh: 她说，无论我们提供多少数据，想要改变彼此的想法都出奇地困难。

sentences.en: But just a little bit of emotion?
sentences.zh: 但如果加入一点点情感呢？

sentences.en: That can go a long way.
sentences.zh: 那可能会产生很大的影响。

sentences.en: Tali Sharot is a cognitive neuroscientist at University College London.
sentences.zh: 塔莉·沙罗特是伦敦大学学院的认知神经科学家。

sentences.en: In her upcoming book, The Influential Mind, she explores how our minds work,
sentences.zh: 在她即将出版的新书《影响力思维》中，她探讨了我们的大脑是如何运作的，

sentences.en: why we ignore the facts, and how you can get people to actually listen to the truth.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们忽视事实，以及你如何才能让人们真正听取真相。

sentences.en: Tali, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 塔莉，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Some months ago, you were listening to a Republican presidential debate,
sentences.zh: 几个月前，你在收听一场共和党总统辩论，

sentences.en: and candidate Donald Trump was asked a question about the safety of childhood vaccines.
sentences.zh: 候选人唐纳德·特朗普被问及关于儿童疫苗安全性的问题。

sentences.en: Here's what he said.
sentences.zh: 他是这样说的。

sentences.en: You take this little, beautiful baby, and you pump.
sentences.zh: 你带着这个小小的、可爱的婴儿，然后注射。

sentences.en: I mean, it looks just like it's meant for a horse, not for a child.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，看起来就像是给马用的，而不是给孩子用的。

sentences.en: And we've had so many instances, people that worked for me, just the other day,
sentences.zh: 我们已经遇到过很多例子，就在前几天，我手下的员工，

sentences.en: two years old, two and a half years old, a child, a beautiful child, went to have the vaccine,
sentences.zh: 两岁，两岁半，一个孩子，一个可爱的孩子，去打了疫苗，

sentences.en: and came back, and a week later got a tremendous fever, got very, very sick, now is autistic.
sentences.zh: 回来后，一周后发了高烧，病得非常非常重，现在患上了自闭症。

sentences.en: Tali, you're a mom, you have two small children.
sentences.zh: 塔莉，你是一位母亲，你有两个年幼的孩子。

sentences.en: At the time Trump said this, one of your kids was two years old, the other was seven weeks old.
sentences.zh: 特朗普说这话时，你的一个孩子两岁，另一个七周大。

sentences.en: Describe your emotional reaction to what he said.
sentences.zh: 描述一下你对他所说的话的情感反应。

sentences.en: Yeah, so when I was listening to Trump at that debate,
sentences.zh: 是的，当我在那场辩论中听特朗普说话时，

sentences.en: I was already quite concerned because I was a mother of a small child,
sentences.zh: 我已经相当担心了，因为我是一个年幼孩子的母亲，

sentences.en: so you're always concerned about the health and safety of your kids,
sentences.zh: 所以你总是会担心孩子的健康和安全，

sentences.en: especially when they're only a few weeks old.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当他们只有几周大的时候。

sentences.en: And so it really tapped into this fear that I had and the anxiety that I already had.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实触动了我内心深处的恐惧和焦虑。

sentences.en: And when he talked about this huge syringe, a horse-sized syringe that was going to go into the baby,
sentences.zh: 当他谈到那个巨大的注射器，那个要扎进婴儿体内的马用注射器时，

sentences.en: in my mind I could imagine the syringe inserted into my small little child
sentences.zh: 我在脑海中想象着注射器扎进我幼小的孩子身上，

sentences.en: and all the bad things that could happen.
sentences.zh: 以及所有可能发生的糟糕事情。

sentences.en: And this was a very irrational reaction on my end because I know that there's not an actual link
sentences.zh: 这对我来说是一种非常不理性的反应，因为我知道自闭症和疫苗之间并没有实际联系，

sentences.en: between autism and vaccines, but it's not enough to have the data.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅有数据是不够的。

sentences.en: Ben Carson, Dr. Ben Carson, was on the other end.
sentences.zh: 本·卡森，本·卡森医生，在另一端。

sentences.en: Well, let me put it this way.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我这样说。

sentences.en: There have been numerous studies, and they have not demonstrated
sentences.zh: 已经有大量的研究，它们并没有证明

sentences.en: that there's any correlation between vaccinations and autism.
sentences.zh: 疫苗接种和自闭症之间有任何相关性。

sentences.en: But that wasn't enough because the data is not enough.
sentences.zh: 但这还不够，因为数据是不够的。

sentences.en: And even if the data is based on very good science,
sentences.zh: 即使这些数据是基于非常好的科学，

sentences.en: it has to be communicated in a way that would really tap into people's needs, their desires.
sentences.zh: 它也必须以一种真正触及人们需求和欲望的方式进行沟通。

sentences.en: If people are afraid, we should address that.
sentences.zh: 如果人们感到害怕，我们应该解决这个问题。

sentences.en: I'm curious, when you sort of contrasted, you know, the weight of the evidence on the one hand
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，当你一方面对比证据的权重，

sentences.en: and this very powerful image of the horse syringe and your seven-week-old baby on the other hand,
sentences.zh: 另一方面对比那个马用注射器的强大意象和你七周大的婴儿时，

sentences.en: how did you talk yourself into trusting the data over that emotional image?
sentences.zh: 你是如何说服自己相信数据而不是那个情感意象的？

sentences.en: What really helped is that I understood what was happening to me.
sentences.zh: 真正有帮助的是我理解了自己身上发生了什么。

sentences.en: You know, the first instinct was like a stress and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 你知道，第一直觉是压力和焦虑。

sentences.en: But because this is what I study, I knew what my reaction was.
sentences.zh: 但因为这就是我的研究领域，我知道我的反应是什么。

sentences.en: I knew where it was coming from.
sentences.zh: 我知道它来自哪里。

sentences.en: I knew how it was going to affect me.
sentences.zh: 我知道它会如何影响我。

sentences.en: And I think that awareness helped me to put it aside and say,
sentences.zh: 我认为这种意识帮助我把它放在一边，并说，

sentences.en: OK, I know that I am anxious for the wrong reasons,
sentences.zh: 好吧，我知道我因为错误的原因感到焦虑，

sentences.en: and this is the action that I should take.
sentences.zh: 这是我应该采取的行动。

sentences.en: It's a little bit when you're on a plane, and there's turbulence, and you get scared.
sentences.zh: 这有点像你在飞机上遇到气流感到害怕的时候。

sentences.en: But telling yourself, I know that turbulence is not actually anything that's dangerous.
sentences.zh: 但告诉自己，我知道气流实际上并没有什么危险。

sentences.en: I know the statistics on safety in planes and so on.
sentences.zh: 我知道关于飞机安全的统计数据等等。

sentences.en: It helps.
sentences.zh: 这有帮助。

sentences.en: It helps people reduce their anxiety.
sentences.zh: 这有助于人们减少焦虑。

sentences.en: The facts don't always relieve our anxieties, though.
sentences.zh: 然而，事实并不总是能缓解我们的焦虑。

sentences.en: Sometimes they only harden our views.
sentences.zh: 有时它们只会加深我们的观点。

sentences.en: Some time ago, Tali did a study where she presented information to people who believe that climate change is real
sentences.zh: 不久前，塔莉做了一项研究，她向相信气候变化是真实存在的人

sentences.en: and to people who are skeptics.
sentences.zh: 以及怀疑论者展示了信息。

sentences.en: She found, for both groups, people strengthened their pre-existing beliefs
sentences.zh: 她发现，对于两组人来说，当新信息证实了他们的想法时，

sentences.en: when new information confirmed what they thought,
sentences.zh: 人们都加强了他们预先存在的信念，

sentences.en: but both groups ignored information when it challenged their views.
sentences.zh: 但两组人在信息挑战他们的观点时都忽略了这些信息。

sentences.en: I asked Tali about this.
sentences.zh: 我问了塔莉关于这件事的看法。

sentences.en: Our psychological biases are the same across individuals, on average.
sentences.zh: 我们的心理偏见在个体之间平均来说是相同的。

sentences.en: We all have what's known as a confirmation bias.
sentences.zh: 我们都有所谓的确认偏见。

sentences.en: A confirmation bias is our tendency to take in any kind of data that confirms our prior convictions
sentences.zh: 确认偏见是我们倾向于接受任何证实我们先前信念的数据，

sentences.en: and to disregard data that does not conform to what we already believe.
sentences.zh: 并忽视那些不符合我们已有信念的数据。

sentences.en: And when we see data that doesn't conform to what we believe,
sentences.zh: 当我们看到不符合我们信念的数据时，

sentences.en: what we do is we try to distance ourselves from it.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的是试图与它保持距离。

sentences.en: We say, well, that data is not credible, right?
sentences.zh: 我们说，嗯，那个数据不可信，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not good evidence for what it's saying.
sentences.zh: 它不能很好地证明它所说的内容。

sentences.en: So we're trying to reframe it, to discredit it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图重新构建它，去质疑它。

sentences.en: I want to sort of push back at you just on one point,
sentences.zh: 我想就一点反驳你，

sentences.en: which is sometimes it seems to me that it actually might be rational to reject data that comes in.
sentences.zh: 那就是有时在我看来，拒绝传入的数据实际上可能是理性的。

sentences.en: You know, if I've seen gravity work all my life, it makes objects fall toward the ground,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我一生都看到重力在起作用，它使物体落向地面，

sentences.en: and you take me into a room where an object seems to be levitating,
sentences.zh: 而你带我进入一个物体似乎在悬浮的房间，

sentences.en: it seems to me the appropriate reaction is not,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，适当的反应不是，

sentences.en: okay, everything I knew about gravity was wrong,
sentences.zh: 好吧，我所知道的关于重力的一切都是错的，

sentences.en: but let me try and understand this anomaly.
sentences.zh: 而是让我试着理解这个异常现象。

sentences.en: Let me try and understand why this object is not doing what it's supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 让我试着理解为什么这个物体没有按照它应该做的那样去做。

sentences.en: It seems to me, and I'm clearly betraying my own beliefs here,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，我显然在这里背叛了我自己的信念，

sentences.en: given the overwhelming weight of evidence that climate change is real,
sentences.zh: 鉴于气候变化是真实存在的压倒性证据，

sentences.en: showing me data that one winter is colder than normal
sentences.zh: 向我展示一个冬天比正常情况更冷的数据

sentences.en: shouldn't make me change my overall view, should it?
sentences.zh: 不应该让我改变我的整体观点，对吧？

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你是绝对正确的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the way that people tend to update their beliefs is that they use the new information
sentences.zh: 所以人们倾向于更新他们信念的方式是，他们使用新信息

sentences.en: in light of what they already believe, because that, on average, is the rational way to go.
sentences.zh: 来对照他们已经相信的东西，因为平均而言，这是理性的做法。

sentences.en: Exactly as you said, when we encounter some kind of information
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，当我们遇到某种信息

sentences.en: that really contradicts what we believe very, very strongly,
sentences.zh: 确实与我们非常强烈相信的东西相矛盾时，

sentences.en: on average, that information is wrong.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，那个信息是错误的。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So I give an example in my book where if someone comes in and says,
sentences.zh: 所以我书里举了一个例子，如果有人进来并说，

sentences.en: I just saw pink elephants flying in the sky,
sentences.zh: 我刚才看到粉红色的象在天空中飞，

sentences.en: and I have a very strong belief, obviously, that no pink elephants fly in the sky,
sentences.zh: 而我有一个非常强烈的信念，显然，没有粉红色的象在天空中飞，

sentences.en: I would then think that they're either delusional or they're lying,
sentences.zh: 那么我会认为他们要么是产生了幻觉，要么是在撒谎，

sentences.en: and there's good reason for me to believe that.
sentences.zh: 我有充分的理由相信这一点。

sentences.en: So it's actually the correct approach to assess data in light of what you believe.
sentences.zh: 所以根据你所相信的东西来评估数据实际上是正确的方法。

sentences.en: There's four factors that determine whether we're going to change our beliefs.
sentences.zh: 有四个因素决定了我们是否会改变我们的信念。

sentences.en: Our old belief, our confidence in that old belief,
sentences.zh: 我们旧的信念，我们对旧信念的信心，

sentences.en: the new piece of data, and our confidence in that piece of data.
sentences.zh: 新的数据，以及我们对那条数据的信心。

sentences.en: And the further away the piece of data is from what you already believe,
sentences.zh: 数据与你已经相信的东西相差越远，

sentences.en: the less likely it is to change your belief.
sentences.zh: 它改变你信念的可能性就越小。

sentences.en: And on average, as you go about the world, that is not a bad approach.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，当你在这个世界上行走时，这不是一种坏方法。

sentences.en: However, it also means that it's really hard to change false beliefs.
sentences.zh: 然而，这也意味着改变错误的信念真的很难。

sentences.en: So if someone holds a belief very strongly, but it is a false belief,
sentences.zh: 所以如果一个人非常强烈地持有某种信念，但那是一个错误的信念，

sentences.en: it's very hard to change it with data.
sentences.zh: 用数据来改变它是非常困难的。

sentences.en: When we come back, we're going to talk about some of the ways
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将讨论一些我们可以重塑他人信念，

sentences.en: we can reshape the beliefs of other people, or our beliefs,
sentences.zh: 或者我们自己信念的方法，

sentences.en: and try and answer the question,
sentences.zh: 并试图回答这个问题，

sentences.en: if throwing good information at people doesn't drive misinformation out of circulation,
sentences.zh: 如果向人们抛出好的信息并不能消除错误信息，

sentences.en: how do you get people to buy the truth?
sentences.zh: 你如何让人们相信真相？

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: It often feels as though fear is used to motivate us to act.
sentences.zh: 人们常常觉得恐惧被用来激励我们采取行动。

sentences.en: The vast majority of Americans today do not feel safe.
sentences.zh: 今天绝大多数美国人感到不安全。

sentences.en: On Sunday, Americans woke up to a nightmare that's become mind-numbingly familiar.
sentences.zh: 周日，美国人在一场变得令人麻木的噩梦中醒来。

sentences.en: This could be the great Trojan horse of all time.
sentences.zh: 这可能是史上最大的特洛伊木马。

sentences.en: Politicians use fear to get us to vote.
sentences.zh: 政客们利用恐惧让我们投票。

sentences.en: TV programs use fear to get us to keep watching.
sentences.zh: 电视节目利用恐惧让我们继续观看。

sentences.en: Public health officials use fear to get us to quit smoking.
sentences.zh: 公共卫生官员利用恐惧让我们戒烟。

sentences.en: I asked Tally whether fear might be an effective way to persuade people to change their minds,
sentences.zh: 我问塔莉，恐惧是否可能是说服人们改变想法的有效方式，

sentences.en: and maybe even their behavior.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是改变他们的行为。

sentences.en: Fear works in two situations.
sentences.zh: 恐惧在两种情况下有效。

sentences.en: It works when people are ready, stressed out,
sentences.zh: 它在人们准备好、压力很大的时候有效，

sentences.en: and it also works when what you're trying to do is get someone not to do something,
sentences.zh: 它在你想做的是让某人不做某事时也有效，

sentences.en: an inaction.
sentences.zh: 一种不作为。

sentences.en: For example, if you try to get someone not to vaccinate their kids, fear may work.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你试图让某人不给他们的孩子接种疫苗，恐惧可能会起作用。

sentences.en: If there's, you know, an apple that looks bad, I don't eat it.
sentences.zh: 如果有一个看起来很坏的苹果，我就不吃它。

sentences.en: Fear is actually not such a good motivator for inducing action,
sentences.zh: 恐惧实际上并不是诱导行动的好动机，

sentences.en: while hope is a better motivator, on average, for motivating action.
sentences.zh: 而希望平均来说是激励行动更好的动机。

sentences.en: You talk about one study in your book where a hospital managed to get its workers to practice hand hygiene,
sentences.zh: 你在书中谈到了一项研究，一家医院设法让其员工练习手部卫生，

sentences.en: to get staff members to wash their hands regularly.
sentences.zh: 让员工定期洗手。

sentences.en: But it turned out the most effective thing wasn't frightening the staff about the risks of transmitting infections.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，最有效的方法不是用传播感染的风险来恐吓员工。

sentences.en: It was something else.
sentences.zh: 而是别的东西。

sentences.en: So in a hospital on the East Coast, a camera was installed to see how often medical staff actually sanitized their hand
sentences.zh: 在东海岸的一家医院，安装了一个摄像头，看看医务人员在进入病房前后

sentences.en: before and after entering a patient's room.
sentences.zh: 实际上多久消毒一次手。

sentences.en: And the medical staff knew that the camera was installed,
sentences.zh: 医务人员知道摄像头已经安装好了，

sentences.en: and yet only one in ten medical staff sanitized their hands before and after entering a patient's room.
sentences.zh: 然而，只有十分之一的医护人员在进出病房前后会进行手部消毒。

sentences.en: But then an intervention was introduced, an electronic board that was put above each door,
sentences.zh: 但后来引入了一项干预措施，在每扇门上方安装了一个电子显示屏，

sentences.en: and it gave the medical staff in real time positive feedback.
sentences.zh: 它能实时给予医护人员积极的反馈。

sentences.en: It showed them the percentage of medical staff that washed their hands in the current shift and the weekly rate as well.
sentences.zh: 它显示了当前轮班中洗手的医护人员比例，以及每周的洗手率。

sentences.en: So anytime a medical staff will wash their hands, the numbers will immediately go up,
sentences.zh: 所以每当有医护人员洗手时，数字就会立即上升，

sentences.en: and there will be a positive feedback saying, you know, good job.
sentences.zh: 并且会显示一条积极的反馈，比如，干得好。

sentences.en: And that affected the likelihood of people washing their hands significantly.
sentences.zh: 这显著影响了人们洗手的可能性。

sentences.en: It went up from 10% to 90%, and it stayed there.
sentences.zh: 比例从10%上升到了90%，并且一直保持在这个水平。

sentences.en: Instead of using the normal approach, instead of saying, you know, you have to wash your hands
sentences.zh: 他们没有使用常规方法，没有说，你知道，你必须洗手，

sentences.en: because otherwise you'll spread the disease,
sentences.zh: 否则你会传播疾病，

sentences.en: basically instead of warning them of all the bad things that can happen in the future,
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们没有警告人们未来可能发生的所有坏事，

sentences.en: which actually results in inaction, they gave them positive feedback.
sentences.zh: 因为那实际上会导致人们不采取行动，而是给予了积极的反馈。

sentences.en: One important idea that Tally has explored is something known as the equality heuristic.
sentences.zh: 塔利（Tally）探索的一个重要理念被称为“平等启发法”。

sentences.en: It's a mental shortcut, and it's really quite simple.
sentences.zh: 这是一种思维捷径，而且非常简单。

sentences.en: We tend to assign equal weight to everyone's opinion.
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于赋予每个人的意见同等的权重。

sentences.en: But sometimes when there's an expert in the room, this mental shortcut can lead us astray.
sentences.zh: 但有时当房间里有专家时，这种思维捷径会把我们引入歧途。

sentences.en: Different people have different expertise,
sentences.zh: 不同的人有不同的专业知识，

sentences.en: and it's better to put more weight on people who are more knowledgeable
sentences.zh: 最好给那些知识更渊博的人更多的权重，

sentences.en: or have more expertise in the domain that we're making the decision in.
sentences.zh: 或者在我们要做出决策的领域拥有更多专业知识的人。

sentences.en: And there's been a study showing that this equality heuristic is something that people do around the world.
sentences.zh: 有一项研究表明，这种平等启发法是世界各地的人们都会使用的方法。

sentences.en: So it's not something that people do only in democratic governments.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是民主政府下人们才会做的事情。

sentences.en: But studies have been conducted in other countries, such as China and Iran,
sentences.zh: 但在其他国家，如中国和伊朗，也进行了相关研究，

sentences.en: and there, too, people go according to the equality heuristic.
sentences.zh: 在那里，人们同样遵循平等启发法。

sentences.en: If they need to make a decision, they will get the opinions of quite a few individuals
sentences.zh: 如果他们需要做出决定，他们会收集相当多人的意见，

sentences.en: and then Tally them up, and that's how they make the decision,
sentences.zh: 然后把它们加总，这就是他们做出决定的方式，

sentences.en: instead of actually using the person in the room who is more knowledgeable and has more expertise.
sentences.zh: 而不是真正利用房间里那个知识更渊博、专业性更强的人。

sentences.en: But how can you know who the expert is?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么知道谁是专家呢？

sentences.en: When your question is about cancer, you can turn to an oncologiSt.
sentences.zh: 当你的问题是关于癌症时，你可以求助于肿瘤学家。

sentences.en: But for other questions, many people might claim to be knowledgeable.
sentences.zh: 但对于其他问题，许多人可能会声称自己知识渊博。

sentences.en: It turns out there's a clever technique to separate the experts from the pretenders.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，有一种巧妙的技术可以将专家与冒充者区分开来。

sentences.en: It's called the surprisingly popular vote.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“出人意料的流行投票”。

sentences.en: Let me show you how it works with an example.
sentences.zh: 让我用一个例子来告诉你它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: I have two questions for you.
sentences.zh: 我有两个问题要问你。

sentences.en: The first is, what's the capital of Brazil?
sentences.zh: 第一个是，巴西的首都是哪里？

sentences.en: Okay, here's a second question.
sentences.zh: 好的，这是第二个问题。

sentences.en: What do you think most people will say is the capital of Brazil?
sentences.zh: 你认为大多数人会说巴西的首都是哪里？

sentences.en: Maybe you thought the capital was Rio de Janeiro.
sentences.zh: 也许你以为首都是里约热内卢。

sentences.en: But maybe you knew the right answer.
sentences.zh: 但也许你知道正确答案。

sentences.en: Brasilia.
sentences.zh: 巴西利亚。

sentences.en: By looking at the results of those two quick polls,
sentences.zh: 通过查看这两个快速民意调查的结果，

sentences.en: I can tell you, with no prior information, that the capital of Brazil is Brasilia.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，在没有任何先验信息的情况下，巴西的首都是巴西利亚。

sentences.en: How would I know that?
sentences.zh: 我怎么会知道呢？

sentences.en: Because if I think Rio de Janeiro is the capital of Brazil,
sentences.zh: 因为如果我认为里约热内卢是巴西的首都，

sentences.en: I will also think that most people think that.
sentences.zh: 我也会认为大多数人是这么想的。

sentences.en: However, if I think Brasilia is the capital of Brazil,
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我认为巴西利亚是巴西的首都，

sentences.en: I will still think that Rio is the answer that most people will give.
sentences.zh: 我仍然会认为里约是大多数人会给出的答案。

sentences.en: So what this ends up being is that Brasilia will be an answer that's more popular than people expect.
sentences.zh: 所以最终的结果是，巴西利亚将是一个比人们预期更受欢迎的答案。

sentences.en: I have to say it took me a minute to understand how this idea works.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我花了一分钟才理解这个想法是如何运作的。

sentences.en: It's complicated, but it really is very clever.
sentences.zh: 它很复杂，但确实非常巧妙。

sentences.en: Here's another example.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个例子。

sentences.en: Let's look at a math problem.
sentences.zh: 让我们看一道数学题。

sentences.en: In a lake, there's a patch of lily pads.
sentences.zh: 在一个湖里，有一片睡莲。

sentences.en: Each day, the patch doubles in size.
sentences.zh: 每天，这片睡莲的面积都会翻倍。

sentences.en: If it takes 48 days for the patch to cover the entire lake,
sentences.zh: 如果这片睡莲覆盖整个湖面需要48天，

sentences.en: how long would it take for the patch to cover half the lake?
sentences.zh: 那么覆盖半个湖面需要多长时间？

sentences.en: The correct answer is 47 days, because the lilies double in area every day.
sentences.zh: 正确答案是47天，因为睡莲每天面积翻倍。

sentences.en: If they fill the lake on day 48, they will fill half the lake on day 47.
sentences.zh: 如果它们在第48天填满湖泊，那么它们在第47天就会填满一半的湖泊。

sentences.en: But the intuitive answer is the 24th day, because 24 is half of 48.
sentences.zh: 但直觉答案是第24天，因为24是48的一半。

sentences.en: If you ask people what the answer is, most people will say 24, a few people will say 47.
sentences.zh: 如果你问人们答案是什么，大多数人会说是24，少数人会说是47。

sentences.en: When you ask people what they think others will say,
sentences.zh: 当你问人们他们认为别人会怎么说时，

sentences.en: nearly everyone will predict that others will say 24.
sentences.zh: 几乎每个人都会预测别人会说24。

sentences.en: Since more people say the answer is 47 than expect others to say the answer is 47,
sentences.zh: 由于说答案是47的人比预期别人会说答案是47的人要多，

sentences.en: 47 turns out to be the surprisingly popular vote answer and the correct one.
sentences.zh: 47就成了“出人意料的流行投票”的答案，也是正确答案。

sentences.en: It's basically a clever way to figure out who has expert or insider information.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一种找出谁拥有专家或内部信息的巧妙方法。

sentences.en: Betting markets work on a similar idea.
sentences.zh: 博彩市场也基于类似的理念。

sentences.en: If there's someone in a group who has knowledge about something
sentences.zh: 如果群体中有人掌握某方面的知识，

sentences.en: and you give them a financial incentive to come forward with that information,
sentences.zh: 而你给予他们经济激励让他们公开这些信息，

sentences.en: you can bring insider information to the surface.
sentences.zh: 你就能挖掘出内部信息。

sentences.en: So the surprising popular vote tends to predict the correct answer in many different domains.
sentences.zh: 所以，“出人意料的流行投票”往往能在许多不同领域预测出正确答案。

sentences.en: It can be factual.
sentences.zh: 它可以是事实性的。

sentences.en: It can be math.
sentences.zh: 它可以是数学问题。

sentences.en: It can be even estimating the price of art.
sentences.zh: 甚至可以是估算艺术品的价格。

sentences.en: So they did a little study where they asked MIT students to estimate the price of art.
sentences.zh: 所以他们做了一个小研究，让麻省理工学院的学生估算艺术品的价格。

sentences.en: Now, MIT students, for the most case, they don't really have a lot of knowledge about art.
sentences.zh: 现在，麻省理工学院的学生，大多数情况下，对艺术并没有太多的了解。

sentences.en: And yet, when they asked them to estimate the price of art
sentences.zh: 然而，当让他们估算艺术品的价格，

sentences.en: and also to say what other people will think about that,
sentences.zh: 并说出其他人会怎么想时，

sentences.en: and they took the surprising popular vote, the surprising popular vote was spot on.
sentences.zh: 他们采用了“出人意料的流行投票”，结果非常准确。

sentences.en: I wrapped up my conversation with Tally by exploring one last idea
sentences.zh: 我通过探索最后一个想法结束了与塔利的谈话，

sentences.en: about how we might convince others to listen to the truth.
sentences.zh: 关于我们如何才能说服他人听取真相。

sentences.en: It had to do with a study of Princeton students who got their brains scanned
sentences.zh: 这与一项普林斯顿大学学生的研究有关，他们的大脑在扫描仪下，

sentences.en: while they listened to a story of a young woman named Annabelle.
sentences.zh: 同时听一个名叫安娜贝尔（Annabelle）的年轻女子的故事。

sentences.en: Producer Renee Klar read an excerpt from that story.
sentences.zh: 制片人蕾妮·克拉（Renee Klar）朗读了那个故事的片段。

sentences.en: I know everyone has some crazy prom stories, but, well, just wait.
sentences.zh: 我知道每个人都有一些疯狂的毕业舞会故事，但是，嗯，等着瞧吧。

sentences.en: I was a freshman in high school in Miami, Florida, and I'm new to the freshman scene.
sentences.zh: 我当时是佛罗里达州迈阿密的一名高中新生，我是新生圈里的新人。

sentences.en: I'm new to the high school scene, I should say.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，我是高中圈里的新人。

sentences.en: And it's almost December, so I've been in high school for about three months.
sentences.zh: 快到十二月了，所以我上高中大约三个月了。

sentences.en: And this boy Charles asks me out.
sentences.zh: 然后这个叫查尔斯（Charles）的男孩约我出去。

sentences.en: He's British, he's a junior, and he's really cute, but sort of shy, but just, well, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 他是英国人，高二学生，真的很可爱，但有点害羞，不过，嗯，这不重要。

sentences.en: So I say yes, I'm excited.
sentences.zh: 所以我答应了，我很兴奋。

sentences.en: The story goes on.
sentences.zh: 故事还在继续。

sentences.en: It includes, as Tally writes, love, rejection, blood, alcohol, and a couple of policemen,
sentences.zh: 正如塔利所写，它包含了爱、拒绝、鲜血、酒精和几个警察，

sentences.en: all the requirements of a bestseller.
sentences.zh: 畅销书的所有要素。

sentences.en: I asked Tally to tell me what happened in the minds of the Princeton students as they listened to that story.
sentences.zh: 我让塔利告诉我，当普林斯顿的学生听那个故事时，他们的大脑里发生了什么。

sentences.en: So this is a study that was conducted by Professor Hassan's group at Princeton.
sentences.zh: 这是一项由普林斯顿大学哈桑（Hassan）教授的研究小组进行的研究。

sentences.en: And what they showed is that when one person listens to another person's story,
sentences.zh: 他们展示的是，当一个人听另一个人的故事时，

sentences.en: the activity in the two brains synchronize.
sentences.zh: 两个大脑中的活动会同步。

sentences.en: So if you're listening to me, then it is possible that the activity of your brain
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在听我说话，那么你的大脑活动就有可能

sentences.en: looks a lot like the activity in my brain.
sentences.zh: 看起来很像我的大脑活动。

sentences.en: And at the beginning, the activity in your brain, listening to my brain,
sentences.zh: 起初，你听我说话时，你大脑中的活动，

sentences.en: it will be delayed in a little bit, right?
sentences.zh: 会有一点延迟，对吧？

sentences.en: So I'm thinking about something, I'm saying the words, you're perceiving the words,
sentences.zh: 我在思考某件事，我在说这些话，你在感知这些话，

sentences.en: and then the activity in your brain will follow the activity in mine.
sentences.zh: 然后你大脑中的活动会跟随我大脑中的活动。

sentences.en: However, they found in that study that after a while,
sentences.zh: 然而，他们在研究中发现，过了一会儿，

sentences.en: the brain of the listener started preceding the brain of the storyteller
sentences.zh: 听者的脑部活动开始领先于讲述者的脑部活动，

sentences.en: because the brain of the listener was predicting what the storyteller will say.
sentences.zh: 因为听者的大脑在预测讲述者接下来要说什么。

sentences.en: So if you looked at the listener brain,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你观察听者的大脑，

sentences.en: you could predict what the activity in Annabelle's brain would look like.
sentences.zh: 你就能预测安娜贝尔大脑中的活动会是什么样子。

sentences.en: But the idea of synchronization seemed to be important for influence.
sentences.zh: 但同步的概念似乎对影响力很重要。

sentences.en: In another study that the same group did,
sentences.zh: 在同一个小组做的另一项研究中，

sentences.en: they found that when people were listening to very strong speeches,
sentences.zh: 他们发现当人们在听非常有力的演讲时，

sentences.en: what they found was the brains of the different people
sentences.zh: 他们发现不同人的大脑

sentences.en: listening to those speeches started synchronizing.
sentences.zh: 在听这些演讲时开始同步。

sentences.en: So if we all listen, for example, to Kennedy's famous moon speech,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们都听，例如，肯尼迪著名的登月演讲，

sentences.en: our brains would likely look very much alike.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑看起来可能会非常相似。

sentences.en: Those who came before us made certain that this country rode the first waves
sentences.zh: 我们之前的人确保了这个国家乘上了工业革命的第一波浪潮，

sentences.en: of the industrial revolution, the first waves of modern invention,
sentences.zh: 现代发明的第一波浪潮，

sentences.en: and the first wave of nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 以及核能的第一波浪潮。

sentences.en: And this generation does not intend to founder in the backwash of the coming age of space.
sentences.zh: 而这一代人并不打算在即将到来的太空时代的余波中沉没。

sentences.en: We mean to be a part of it.
sentences.zh: 我们打算成为其中的一部分。

sentences.en: We mean to lead it.
sentences.zh: 我们打算引领它。

sentences.en: And this is not only in regions that are important for language and hearing,
sentences.zh: 这不仅是在对语言和听力重要的区域，

sentences.en: it's also in regions that are important for emotion,
sentences.zh: 它也在对情绪重要的区域，

sentences.en: in regions that are important for what's known as fear of mind,
sentences.zh: 在对所谓的“心智理论”重要的区域，

sentences.en: our ability to think about what other people are thinking,
sentences.zh: 即我们思考别人在想什么的能力，

sentences.en: in regions that are important for associations.
sentences.zh: 以及在对联想重要的区域。

sentences.en: And you try to think, well, what's common to all these influential speeches
sentences.zh: 你试着去想，嗯，所有这些有影响力的演讲有什么共同点，

sentences.en: that can cause so many people's activity to synchronize?
sentences.zh: 能导致这么多人的活动同步？

sentences.en: And one of the most important things is emotion.
sentences.zh: 其中最重要的一点就是情绪。

sentences.en: If the storyteller or the person giving the speech is able to elicit emotion in the other person,
sentences.zh: 如果讲述者或演讲者能够激发对方的情绪，

sentences.en: then he's actually having somewhat of a control on that person's state of mind.
sentences.zh: 那么他实际上就在某种程度上控制了那个人的精神状态。

sentences.en: So think about it like this.
sentences.zh: 所以这样想。

sentences.en: If you're very sad and I'm telling you a joke, well, you're sad.
sentences.zh: 如果你很伤心，而我给你讲个笑话，嗯，你还是很伤心。

sentences.en: So you're not going to perceive the joke as I perceive it when I'm happy.
sentences.zh: 所以你不会像我快乐时那样去感知这个笑话。

sentences.en: But if I'm able to first make you happy and then tell you the joke,
sentences.zh: 但如果我能先让你快乐，然后再给你讲那个笑话，

sentences.en: well, then you perceive it more from my point of view.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那你就会更多地从我的角度去感知它。

sentences.en: So by eliciting emotion, what you're able to do is change the perception of everything that comes after,
sentences.zh: 所以通过激发情绪，你能够做的是改变对之后一切事物的感知，

sentences.en: to perceive information as the person who's giving the speech wants you to perceive it.
sentences.zh: 从而按照演讲者希望你感知的方式去感知信息。

sentences.en: So you can see how this coupling, this idea that the audience's mind and the speaker's mind
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到这种耦合，这种听众的思想和演讲者的思想

sentences.en: are in some ways coupled together, you can see how this could potentially be used to spread good information.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上耦合在一起的想法，你可以看到这如何可能被用来传播好的信息。

sentences.en: You know, you have a great teacher in high school and you're captivated by the teacher
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在高中有一位伟大的老师，你被这位老师吸引，

sentences.en: and you're being pulled along by the story the teacher is telling you,
sentences.zh: 你被老师讲的故事所牵引，

sentences.en: maybe about history or maybe about geography.
sentences.zh: 也许是关于历史，也许是关于地理。

sentences.en: But you can also see equally how the same thing can work in the opposite direction,
sentences.zh: 但你同样可以看到同样的事情如何以相反的方向运作，

sentences.en: that you could be listening to a demagogue or you could be listening to somebody
sentences.zh: 你可能在听一个煽动者，或者你可能在听某个人，

sentences.en: who has a very sort of captivating rhetorical style.
sentences.zh: 他有一种非常引人入胜的修辞风格。

sentences.en: And this person could also lead you astray in just the same way that the great teacher
sentences.zh: 而这个人也可能把你引入歧途，就像那位伟大的老师

sentences.en: can lead you to knowledge and to positive things.
sentences.zh: 可以引导你走向知识和积极的事物一样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: All the different factors that affect whether we will be influenced by one person
sentences.zh: 所有影响我们是否会被一个人影响

sentences.en: or ignore another person are the same,
sentences.zh: 或忽视另一个人的不同因素都是一样的，

sentences.en: whether the person has good intentions or bad intentions, right?
sentences.zh: 无论此人是心怀善意还是恶意，对吧？

sentences.en: The factors that affect whether you're influential can be,
sentences.zh: 影响你是否具有影响力的一些因素可能是，

sentences.en: can you elicit emotion in the other person?
sentences.zh: 你能否激发对方的情绪？

sentences.en: Can you tell a story?
sentences.zh: 你会讲故事吗？

sentences.en: Are you taking into account the state of mind of the person that's in front of you?
sentences.zh: 你是否考虑到了你面前那个人的心态？

sentences.en: Are you giving them data that confirms to their preconceived notions?
sentences.zh: 你提供的数据是否符合他们先入为主的观念？

sentences.en: All those factors that make one speech more influential than the other
sentences.zh: 所有那些使一场演讲比另一场更具影响力，

sentences.en: or more likely to create an impact can be used for good and can be used for bad.
sentences.zh: 或更有可能产生影响的因素，既可以用于善，也可以用于恶。

sentences.en: And Tali Sharad, I want to thank you for joining me on Hidden Brain today.
sentences.zh: 塔莉·沙拉，感谢你今天来到《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: This week's episode was produced by Maggie Penman and Raina Cohen
sentences.zh: 本周的节目由玛吉·彭曼和蕾娜·科恩制作，

sentences.en: and edited by Tara Boyle.
sentences.zh: 并由塔拉·博伊尔编辑。

sentences.en: A special shout out to our former intern, Chloe Connolly,
sentences.zh: 特别感谢我们以前的实习生克洛伊·康诺利，

sentences.en: who interviewed the liberals and conservatives we heard at the start of this episode.
sentences.zh: 她采访了我们在本集开头听到的那些自由派和保守派人士。

sentences.en: Our staff includes Jenny Schmidt, Parth Shah, and Renee Klar.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作人员包括珍妮·施密特、帕斯·沙阿和蕾妮·克拉尔。

sentences.en: This week, our unsung hero is Brian Moffitt of National Public Media.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们默默无闻的英雄是来自国家公共媒体的布莱恩·莫菲特。

sentences.en: NPM is the group that sells our sponsorship messages.
sentences.zh: NPM 是负责销售我们赞助信息的团队。

sentences.en: Brian is a great mix of liberal and conservative.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩是一个自由派和保守派的完美结合体。

sentences.en: He's always liberal in his encouragement and conservative in his promises.
sentences.zh: 他在鼓励他人时总是很“自由派”，而在做出承诺时却很“保守”。

sentences.en: As the saying goes, he under-promises and over-delivers.
sentences.zh: 正如俗话所说，他承诺得少，做得多。

sentences.en: Thanks, Brian.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，布莱恩。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆，这里是 NPR。
